title: test: cover the wrapper self-restart hand-over in both postflight harnesses
description:
FOLLOW-UP to df42861 (governor fix, 2026-09-18). The wrapper self-restart — the top-of-loop check that relaunches when the wrapper's own bytes change on disk — has NO harness or parity coverage in either twin. `grep -n 'source changed on disk' scripts/tests/*` returns nothing today.

That gap let a real defect live: the ps1 path relaunched via `Start-Process`, which gave the new wrapper its own console window and left the launching terminal at a prompt. Operators read that as a dead seat and relaunched the same worker id, so two wrapper loops shared one seat and two CLIs reviewed task-49ec8755 at the same time (2026-09-18, qa-a36819c3 and worker-d0c3b06e). df42861 hands over with the call operator instead, past the outer finally, and deregisters with reason `wrapper_restart` first, matching the sh twin's `exec`.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE CARD: scripts/tests/postflight.{sh,ps1} were held by task-e47284ef when the fix landed, and task-32ecce5d has the same files next. Adding the case then would have been swept into another task's commit.

WHAT TO ASSERT (daemon-free, in the existing fake-proxy harness): with the wrapper copy's bytes changed between iterations, the run must show exactly one `deregister_worker` RPC carrying reason `wrapper_restart`, then a fresh registration from the relaunched wrapper, and exactly one restart per on-disk change (the relaunched process re-reads the hash and must not thrash). The engine difference is the hand-over mechanism itself, so assert what both twins share — the RPC sequence — rather than pids. On ps1 the relaunch is a child of the wrapper and inherits its console; on sh `exec` replaces the process, so the pid is unchanged.

SUGGESTED PROOF (the worker decides): revert the call operator to `Start-Process` in a scratch copy and show the case turns red, the same way the other harness mutations are proven.
definitionOfDone: Both scripts/tests/postflight.sh and scripts/tests/postflight.ps1 gain a self-restart case: change the wrapper copy's bytes between iterations and assert one deregister_worker with reason 'wrapper_restart', a fresh registration afterwards, and exactly one restart per on-disk change.
The case is proven RED on a scratch copy that restores the pre-df42861 behaviour (Start-Process relaunch, deregister reason terminal_closed).
MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh and the ps1 twin both pass on a quiet box, and parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 stay green.
Any new banner or reason literal is registered in both parity checkers' fixed lists.
taskRails: Harness-only change; scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and scripts/moe-agent.sh stay as df42861 left them unless the case proves them wrong.
Keep both harness twins byte-identical in the shared fake-proxy JavaScript, as the surrounding cases already require.

comments.content:
SELF-REVIEW (worker-c1d9de02, adversarial-self-review). This card carries NO file edits, so the diff under review is empty and the review covers the claims instead.

1. Vacuous pass? No. sh arm (postflight.sh ~1891-1932): reload_wait needs the RPC sequence to reach '^c+rcc', then '^c+rc{2,}rcc', then end as '^c+rc{2,}rc{2,}$'. An inert restart never produces an `r`, so it times out with 'timed out after Ns waiting for ...'. It fails fast on `x` ('a deregister other than wrapper_restart'), on more restarts than edits ('a restart with no edit behind it') and on wrapper exit. ps1 arm (postflight.ps1 ~1698-1790): Wait-ReloadSequence '^c+rc' then '^c+rc+rc', final '^c+rc+rc+$', and pass 2 must run the edited bytes. The step-2 mutants proved it: ARGV gave 'cr', S1 gave 'cx' and S2 gave 'r', and each was RED with its own line.

2. Do the red proofs cover both incidents? Yes. ps1 pre-df42861 (Start-Process relaunch + default terminal_closed) went RED on PS 5.1.26100.9711 and pwsh 7.6.8 with `HOT RELOAD FAILED: no claim after reload 1 (... RPC sequence 'cx')`. That is the 2026-09-18 double-seat shape. sh ARGV mutant, `the wrapper exited (RPC sequence 'cr')`, covers 'every sh seat dies on first reload'. Parity bite: renaming wrapper_restart in the sh wrapper alone fails parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 on both engines.

3. Anything written outside scratch? No. All work ran in `git archive HEAD scripts` copies, under a unique native-fs dir for sh and a unique /mnt/d/moe-scratch dir for ps1. Both are removed. `git status --short` over the six step-1 paths shows only ` M scripts/tests/postflight.sh`, which was a peer's (5f3960df) edit before this task began; I did not touch it. `git diff --quiet 23df1bf HEAD` over the six paths exits 0, so the verified snapshot matches the current HEAD bc45829.

4. Platforms. Linux sh: parity-check.sh PASS, postflight.sh exit 0 (73 frozen, '[hot reload] ok: 2 restarts, each re-registered, none without an edit', scope 36). PS 5.1.26100.9711: parity PASS and postflight.ps1 exit 0 (73 frozen, '[hot reload] ok: 2 reloads, 1 wrapper process, 1 runner identity', scope 36). pwsh 7.6.8: the same. NOT covered, by design: stock macOS without sha256sum has the sh reload off (fail-open); I noted it and did not fix it. Also not covered: ps1 through node->powershell, CI's 5.1 leg. The ps1 runs launched powershell.exe directly from WSL.

5. Rail. Fake-proxy bodies at HEAD (BOM/CRLF-normalized): sh 7c3afb75db6cb47069e9897b1254c9fa5c7ea71deac095c835f4acd4801955ba (32746 B), ps1 caf7a0b096d1c801f0800327bc77a2666afb5e7ba9b2b1682b76ce38a9adc304 (31418 B). Both are identical to the b35d46c hashes, so there is no new divergence. This card added no fake-proxy bytes. The twins already differ from each other (mem gotcha-postflight-fake-proxy-twins-diverged). prop-0da6d575 (MODIFY_RAIL) is pending with the human; reconciliation is LOW BACKLOG row task-7c2872e7052646b7a521cb7a8f01c546.

6. Deviation to flag for QA: MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=400 was used instead of the DoD's 180. The box was not quiet (load 11-18 on 16 cores, three peer full harnesses running), and 400 only widens the per-wrapper wait bound. No scenario was retried and none failed, so I do not expect a quiet-box rerun at 180 to differ, but I did not run it at 180.

Board note: this card ships no edits; the wrappers land only its task record. Its old dependency on task-07474ee4 was dropped on 2026-10-25 for lack of file overlap, and no dependency on task-5f3960df is needed since nothing here edits postflight.{sh,ps1}.

implementationPlan.description:
VERIFY IN PLACE (read-only, no edit). Everything this card builds is already in HEAD of moe/work-2026-10-24. It was ported by the integration squash 5e74fb8 "Integrate all Moe work and prompt caching (#194)". The original commits are on the old branch, not in HEAD: cd6bdee (sh case + parity), 45633c7 (sh argv fix), 021f351/469ed6d (task-84150869's ps1 arm). Prove each DoD artifact by anchor, never by line number. The tree drifts, and 5f3960df/07474ee4 also edit these files:
(1) scripts/tests/postflight.sh has the '[hot reload] a changed wrapper restarts once per edit and re-registers' case, with its c/r/x mapping, its fail-fast checks (x, more restarts than edits, 'the wrapper exited'), its quiet windows (^c+rcc, ^c+rc{2,}rcc, final ^c+rc{2,}rc{2,}$) and its 'edit 1 loaded' check, ending at '[hot reload] ok: 2 restarts, each re-registered, none without an edit'.
(2) scripts/moe-agent.sh captures MOE_WRAPPER_ARGV=("$@") ABOVE '# Parse arguments', so the self-restart re-execs with the launch argv.
(3) scripts/tests/postflight.ps1 has task-84150869's arm ('Hot reload keeps ONE wrapper process'): two edits to a copied wrapper, the c/r/x mapping, the sequence '^c+rc+rc+$', exactly one wrapper process after each reload, and the edit-1 announcement.
(4) Both parity checkers have the 'hot reload' group with 'wrapper source changed on disk; restarting to load it' and 'wrapper_restart'.
(5) The shared fake-proxy JavaScript is byte-identical in both harnesses: extract and cmp it.
Note each item as 'NO EDIT MADE — outcome already present from 5e74fb8, verified in place', with the grep command and its result (mem pattern-verify-a-stale-task-instead-of-redoing-it). This plan has NO file edits. If any artifact is missing or wrong, STOP and call moe.request_replan with the evidence. Do not edit harness or wrapper files under this verification-only plan.

RED PROOFS (DoD 2), only in scratch copies of a HEAD snapshot of scripts/, never the shared checkout:
cp -R scripts /mnt/d/moe-scratch/<unique>/ for ps1 (a Windows-drive cwd is needed, see below); a native-fs copy for sh.
(a) ps1, literally pre-df42861. df42861 is in HEAD: read `git show df42861 -- scripts/moe-agent.ps1` and restore its pre-change hand-over in the COPIED moe-agent.ps1. Replace today's restart hand-over (task-84150869's in-process supervisor rerun / call operator, with Invoke-MoeDeregister -Reason 'wrapper_restart') with the old Start-Process relaunch and the default 'terminal_closed' deregister. Run the copied postflight.ps1 on Windows PowerShell 5.1: from WSL, powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File 'D:\moe-scratch\<unique>\scripts\tests\postflight.ps1'. Use a /mnt/d cwd, env -u for every MOE_* and CLAUDE_* variable, MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180, and `| tr -d '\0'` (mem gotcha-qa-ps1-postflight-from-wsl). It must FAIL at the hot-reload arm with 'HOT RELOAD FAILED' naming an 'x' in the RPC sequence. Repeat on pwsh 7 when `command -v pwsh pwsh.exe` finds one; otherwise state that pwsh 7 is unavailable here (CI runs both engines on Windows).
(b) sh, using the subset harness built by anchors (mem gotcha-shared-tree-long-harness-needs-snapshot: source up to FROZEN_SUITE=..., resumed after the MOE_FROZEN_TEST_ONLY exit line). Three mutants of the copied moe-agent.sh: ARGV moves the MOE_WRAPPER_ARGV capture back below the option parser (expect 'the wrapper exited' with sequence 'cr' after 'Provide --project or --project-name'); S1 deregisters the restart with reason terminal_closed (expect 'cx'); S2 makes the launch hash never match, e.g. hash /dev/null (expect a restart with no edit, 'r'). Each must FAIL with its expected 'HOT RELOAD FAILED' line, and the unmutated copy must PASS.
(c) Parity bite: rename wrapper_restart in the copied moe-agent.sh only. parity-check.sh and parity-check.ps1 (PS 5.1), run from that scratch root, must both FAIL and name it.
Paste every failure line. If any proof stays GREEN, STOP and request_replan with the evidence. Error handling: every wait is bounded, and every scratch dir is unique and removed afterwards.

FULL VERIFICATION (DoD 3), run sequentially on a quiet box from a FRESH snapshot of HEAD's scripts/, because peers edit the live tree. The harness derives ROOT_DIR/$root from its own location, so a directory holding only scripts/ is a complete root.
1. `bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh` PASS, and parity-check.ps1 on PS 5.1 (and pwsh 7 if present) PASS.
2. Completion evidence: `MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_SEC=180 bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh` exits 0 in WSL/Linux (CI runs it on ubuntu). Copy the snapshot to the native filesystem, scrub MOE_*/CLAUDE_* with env -u, start it with run_in_background and wait with a bounded Monitor/poll, never a foreground sleep. It takes roughly 20-50 minutes. Its command, exitCode and outputTail go into complete_task.verification.
3. postflight.ps1 on PS 5.1 PASS via the recipe in step 2(a), using the unmutated snapshot. Do the same on pwsh 7 when available; otherwise say so.
If a frozen-suite or unrelated scenario fails, rerun it once. If it reproduces, run the same snapshot's PARENT revision before blaming anything. Report it honestly by name, with no skips and no weakening. affectedFiles is empty on purpose: this task changes no file.

SELF-REVIEW, posted as a task comment (load adversarial-self-review). Questions:
1. Can the cases pass vacuously? Every stage needs an observed c or r, so an inert restart times out.
2. Do the red proofs cover both incidents? The ps1 Start-Process/terminal_closed proof covers the 2026-09-18 double seat. The sh ARGV proof covers 'every sh seat dies on first reload'.
